BitStatusUtil.add:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Merges a new status flag into an existing bitmask by validating both values and returning their bitwise OR." add]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> states </REF>: integer "Existing bitmask representing accumulated status flags; if 0, the result equals stat exactly"
        <REF> stat </REF>: integer "Status bit or bitmask to merge in; if 0, the result equals states unchanged"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: integer "Bitwise OR of states and stat, representing the union of all set flags from both operands"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Call BitStatusUtil.check with a list containing both states and stat to validate that both arguments are legitimate bitmask values RESULT validation_result]
            [COMMAND Compute the bitwise OR of states and stat, combining all set bits from both operands into a single integer, then return that value to the caller RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
BitStatusUtil.has:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Checks whether all bits specified by a status flag are present in a composite bitmask by validating inputs and performing a bitwise subset test." has]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> states </REF>: int "A bitmask integer representing a composite set of active status flags; expected to be non-negative."
        <REF> stat </REF>: int "A single status flag or multi-bit mask to test for presence; expected to be a non-zero power-of-two constant or intentional multi-bit mask."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: bool "True if every bit set in stat is also set in states; false otherwise. Always true when stat is zero."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Call BitStatusUtil.check passing the list [states, stat] to validate that both inputs satisfy preconditions for a bitwise status check. RESULT validation_complete]
            [COMMAND Compute the bitwise AND of states and stat, then compare the result to stat; return true if they are equal, indicating that all bits of stat are present in states, otherwise return false. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: stat equals zero]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND The bitwise AND of any states value with zero is zero, which equals stat (zero), so the expression evaluates to true regardless of the value of states; return true. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: states equals zero and stat is non-zero]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND The bitwise AND of zero with any non-zero stat is zero, which does not equal stat, so the expression evaluates to false; return false. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: stat has multiple bits set (e.g., stat equals 0x06)]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Perform the same bitwise AND and equality check; return true only if all bits of the multi-bit mask are simultaneously present in states, otherwise return false. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
BitStatusUtil.remove:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Removes a bit flag from a status bitmask by XOR-ing it out, but only if the flag is currently set, returning the original bitmask unchanged if the flag is absent." remove]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> states </REF>: int "The current bitmask representing a collection of active status flags"
        <REF> stat </REF>: int "The single bit flag or multi-bit mask to remove from states"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: int "The updated bitmask with stat cleared if it was present, or the original states value if stat was not present"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Validate that both states and stat are legal bitmask values by calling BitStatusUtil.check with the two-element sequence [states, stat]; this is a guard that raises or short-circuits on invalid input before any mutation is attempted RESULT _validation_done]
            [COMMAND Test whether the flag stat is currently active in states by calling BitStatusUtil.has(states, stat); the result is true when at least one bit of stat is present in states and false otherwise RESULT _flag_is_present]
            [COMMAND If _flag_is_present is true, compute states XOR stat to clear exactly the bits represented by stat from states and return that value immediately as an early exit, bypassing all remaining steps RESULT _early_return_value]
            [COMMAND If _flag_is_present was false, fall through to this step and return the original states value unchanged RESULT _fallthrough_return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: stat is not set in states, i.e., BitStatusUtil.has(states, stat) returns false]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Skip the XOR operation entirely and return states as-is, preserving the bitmask without modification RESULT _fallthrough_return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
BitStatusUtil.check:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Validates that every value in the args collection is a non-negative even integer, raising a ValueError immediately on the first value that is either negative or odd." check]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> args </REF>: iterable "A collection of values to validate; each element is expected to be a numeric integer"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Iterate over each element in args, processing one element at a time in sequence RESULT arg]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop, check whether the current element arg is strictly less than 0 RESULT negativity_check]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop, if the negativity check passes (arg is not negative), check whether arg is odd by evaluating arg modulo 2 is not equal to 0 RESULT parity_check]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: Within the for loop, the current element arg is less than 0 (exclusive lower bound: zero itself passes)]
        [LOG "The value that failed the negativity check is identified by its own value in the error message"]
        [THROW ValueError "Raised immediately with the message '{arg} must be greater than or equal to 0'; no further elements are processed after this point"]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: Within the for loop, the current element arg is not negative but arg modulo 2 is not equal to 0 (i.e., arg is odd)]
        [LOG "The value that failed the parity check is identified by its own value in the error message"]
        [THROW ValueError "Raised immediately with the message '{arg} not even'; no further elements are processed after this point"]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
